newsitem.title: FRANCE: BNP, Dresdner stick to holdings.
newsitem.headline: BNP, Dresdner stick to holdings.

text.p: Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) and German partner Dresdner Bank do not have any short term plans to raise their cross-shareholdings, even if a cooperation pact allows for it, BNP chairman Michel Pebereau said on Monday.
"They (the holdings) come to a little less than one percent in the capital of each bank. We do not plan for that to change in the near future," Pebereau told reporters.
A cooperation pact between the banks allows them to raise cross-holdings to 10 percent, but gives no timeframe.
Asked about the possibility of the merger, Pebereau was elusive.
"Our cooperation in the future could involve a wide range of developments...closer ties is one of many alternatives which could crop up in five years, 10 years, 20 or 50 years," he said.
